text:
Aisha K.: Hey folks, running into two odd behaviors on Windows + Python 3.10/3.11 with the python SDK: intermittent certificate verification failures when using system cert store, and separately, the AsyncClient will hang during background token refresh when concurrent requests are inflight. repro steps below.

Ben T.: can you share a minimal repro? usually these are env var precedence or event loop interactions.

Aisha K.: Minimal snippet:```py
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient
import certifi

async def worker():
    c = AsyncClient(api_key="@token@")
    for _ in range(20):
        await c.generate("test")

async def main():
    await asyncio.gather(*(worker() for _ in range(4)))

asyncio.run(main())
```
Run on windows-latest, venv, pip-installed certifi. It sometimes raises ssl.SSLError: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED, other times the process hangs without stack traces while auth refresh is logged.

Camille R.: What's the auth flow? are you using short-lived tokens + background refresh? any proxies?

Aisha K.: Yes, app uses short-lived tokens and we enable auto-refresh (default). No corporate proxy. Logs show: `auth: starting refresh`, `ssl: handshake start`, and then nothing. Attaching a log snippet.

Dev CI Bot: Uploaded logs to /artifacts/ci-1890011223/logs.tar.gz

Egor P.: Two likely issues: 1) on Windows the SSL_CERT_FILE vs system store precedence is ambiguous in our wrapper, 2) token refresh uses a shared async lock incorrectly so multiple coroutines race to refresh and some block indefinitely when handshake-level sockets deadlock.

Aisha K.: I tried setting SSL_CERT_FILE to certifi.where() and that reduces verifier errors but then the hang still occurs when refresh overlaps with heavy concurrency.

Ben T.: Plan: (a) enforce explicit env var precedence: SSL_CERT_FILE > REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE > ca_bundle arg > certifi > windows store, (b) add a per-client asyncio.Lock around refresh so only one inflight refresh happens, (c) improve socket timeouts and ensure handshake cancellations wake waiting tasks. I'll open an issue and a small patch.

Camille R.: Please include a tiny windows CI job that runs the repro for a few seconds to catch regressions. Also add a doc note for users on Windows about setting SSL_CERT_FILE if using custom CA.

Egor P.: I'll PR a test that runs on python 3.10 and 3.11 matrix on windows-latest with reduced iterations to avoid long CI runtime.

Aisha K.: Thanks. For workaround, folks can pass `ca_bundle=certifi.where()` and `refresh_tokens=False` for now, or set SSL_CERT_FILE. Would be great to also surface a warning when we detect mixed cert sources.

Ben T.: Filing GH issue now. @Dev CI Bot can you create redwood/redwood-py issue with labels windows, ssl, async, sdk?

Dev CI Bot: Created issue redwood/redwood-py#442: "Windows: intermittent CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED + AsyncClient hang during concurrent token refresh" — https://github.com/redwood/redwood-py/issues/442

Aisha K.: Appreciate the quick turnaround. I'll validate the PR on our end once ready. :thumbsup:
